key_insight: PFedQFT combines reusable compact adapters with local personalization to reduce federated fine-tuning overhead while maintaining competitive performance on most evaluated medical tasks.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help institutions collaboratively adapt medical LLMs without transferring raw records while accommodating differences in local data.
method: Constructs reusable orthonormal adaptation bases from compact skew-symmetric generators using an approximate matrix exponential and QR orthonormalization.
Shares bases across compatible Transformer projections and uses a globally shared full core.
Adds lightweight private residual operators with globally learned directions and locally retained coefficients.
evidence_signal: Experiments on seven public medical tasks and multiple LLM backbones showed substantial reductions in trainable parameters and per-round adapter uploads, with competitive predictive performance on most tasks.
watch_item: Public-task results do not establish clinical readiness, and keeping raw records local does not by itself guarantee privacy.
paper_title: PFedQFT: Personalized Federated Quantum-Inspired Fine-Tuning for Medical Large Language Models
